requirement: If every `vet_answer` callback invoked by {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.agent-calls.vet_answer` returns `Ok(VetResult::Accept)`, or the request has no callbacks, the answer is successfully submitted and the agent conversation ends.
rationale:
The requirement `requirements.sdk.graph.agent-calls.vet_answer.ok` has two testable obligations. When every callback returns `Accept`, the answer is submitted and the conversation ends. When the request has no callbacks, the same happens. I read both marked tests and did not request any implementation source.

- **All callbacks accept:** `crates/trust-budy-verify` is not involved. The test is `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/tests.rs#fn[vetting_collects_corrections_and_rechecks_every_callback]`. It registers three callbacks, one before and two after `contents_of_current_node`, so both builder phases are exercised. The first submission (`false`) is corrected. On the second submission (`true`) all three callbacks return `Accept`. The test asserts that the awaited `Ask` returns `Ok` with `true`. It asserts that `seen == [false, true]`, so the first callback is re-run on every submission. It also asserts that exactly 2 requests were made, so the conversation ended at acceptance and no further turn was started.
- **No callbacks:** `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/tests.rs#fn[one_submission_accepts_only_its_value_and_skips_other_calls_and_prose]` calls `ctx.ask::<bool>()` with no `vet_answer`. It asserts that the submitted `false` is returned as `Ok`. It asserts that exactly 1 request was made, so the conversation ended after the submission. It also asserts that the other tool call in the same turn was not executed.

I found no input class that the requirement distinguishes and the tests miss. Accepting on the first submission with callbacks present is the same behaviour as the final acceptance in the first test. Both tests carry `{test}` references to the subject, so there is no marking gap.
